notes: Building and Engineering News, vol. 18 part 1 (Internet Archive buildingengineer1818cont), the 26 weekly issues from 2 January to 26 June 1918. Same method as the later volumes: every numbered entry under Building Permit Applications and Building Contracts was taken from the djvu.xml OCR, East Bay headings set aside, and each San Francisco lot built from the block corner on the DPW street centrelines and compared with the sf-parcels shapes; a placement was accepted where the lot starts within two feet of a lot line of today (or the record names an unambiguous corner) and the roll dates the building 1917-1920, and alterations were matched by printed street number in sf-eas-addresses where the roll dates the building before 1918. The labels are printed with a row of leader dots ('Owner........'), which extract.py reads since the January to June 1919 volume. Most items are printed twice in the volume, so the 1,720 entries stand for about 1,100 numbered items; where both printings of a permit were placed, the later one is left out as a repeat (two cases, one of them a permit the paper corrected from six apartments to four flats). Every published row was read against the page image, location first; most of the 103 rows read needed a name, a cost or the wording corrected, and a cost or name that could not be read on the image was left out. Entries cut by a column break were read on in the next column. Descriptions of rows marked confidence low were built from the OCR and have not been read against the image. Owners are private individuals and are cut everywhere (raw.note; scrub_owner.py removes the fragments the OCR garbles past the first cut); a firm or institution named as owner is kept, and where the contractor, architect or engineer named is the owner, shares the owner's surname or is listed at the owner's premises that name is cut too. Sub-trade contracts are timeline entries and set no builder credit. Completion notices, liens, sub-contracts printed 'on above' and the news columns were not taken. The paper came out on Wednesdays; issue dates are set from the cover dates (issues.json beside the corpus: first leaf of each issue, set by hand from the cover line or from the masthead four leaves after it), and the item numbers rise issue by issue under those dates. Item numbers run on from 1917 in the first issue and restart with the issue of 9 January. Three single houses that were read against the image and have no architect left to name sit with the held single houses. One held alteration of a later volume (65 Battery Street, June 1930) whose parcel got a page from this volume was read against the image and published in its own file.

coverage.remaining: Vols. 18 pt. 1 to 31 read (January 1918 to January 1932); the 6 half-year volumes before 1918 (1915 to 1917) are unread, buildingengineer1727cont (July to December 1917) next. In this volume: 82 rows placed on a parcel whose roll year fits, single houses with no architect named and no page, are logged and held until another fact gives the parcel a page (extra.placed_apn; all but three still need the image check). 303 rows have a nearest parcel that was not accepted (the lot starts off today's lot lines, or the roll dates the building outside the window). 501 rows were not placed: location lines not parsed (tract lots, garbled headings), street pairs that do not cross under the names read, and printed street numbers with no EAS row today.
coverage.note: 1,720 numbered entries read, 986 San Francisco rows, 485 placed on a parcel, 103 picked and read against the page image, 70 published on 66 pages (31 seeded), 30 held back: 13 storeys, unit counts or uses that contradict the roll, eight pieces of minor work, seven alterations with nothing to confirm the street number and two repeat listings; three more joined the held houses.
